global_caveat: Every price anchor in this audit comes from a single agency blog post publishing its own asking prices. It is not a market survey, a transaction dataset, or an independent benchmark. Present it as 'what one agency publicly asks', never as 'the market rate'. A client who pushes on this is right to.

anchors.label: AI audit gateway
anchors.note: This is the price of the product you are holding.

archetypes.name: Accountable delivery
archetypes.what_changes: You stop selling the artifact and start selling ownership of the execution, with an SLA and a consequence attached.
archetypes.evidence_note: Rests on the argument that AI plans confidently and executes badly, so accountability is the scarce good. Reasoning, not measurement.

archetypes.name: Outcome ownership
archetypes.what_changes: Priced on a realized result with a defined metric, baseline, window and attribution rule. You carry downside.
archetypes.evidence_note: Outcome pricing is documented as the direction of travel, and WPP ties 20-25% of fees to performance. Whether it works for a small agency is not established anywhere in the corpus.

archetypes.name: Strategy and positioning
archetypes.what_changes: Sell the judgment layer: what to build, for whom, and what not to do. The part AI plans badly and cannot be held to.
archetypes.evidence_note: That strategy retains value is well supported. NO PRICE ANCHOR EXISTS in the corpus for strategy work. Any number quoted here would be invented.

archetypes.name: Productized AI line
archetypes.what_changes: Not a repricing of existing work. A new line sold at published AI-services prices.
archetypes.evidence_note: Prices are documented as asking prices from one source. Demand at those prices is not established.
